title: 2012 AMC 8 Problem 17
statement: A square with an integer side length is cut into \(10\) squares, all of which have integer side length and at least \(8\) of which have area \(1.\) What is the smallest possible value of the length of the side of the original square?

solutions.text:
Since all \(10\) squares have positive integer side lengths, each has area at least \(1\). Their total area is therefore at least \(10\). A square with integer side length at most \(3\) has area at most \(3^2=9\), so its side length cannot be less than \(4\).

The following configuration cuts a \(4\times4\) square into ten integer-sided squares, eight of which are unit squares. Therefore side length \(4\) is attainable and is the minimum.

Thus, the answer is B .
hints: A side length of \(3\) gives area too small for ten integer squares.
A \(4\) by \(4\) square can be cut as shown.
